question: Can I build up unused FHSA participation room in years before I open my first FHSA?
generated_answer:
Yes, you can build up unused FHSA participation room in years before you open your first FHSA. This is because the 10% limit on FHSA contributions applies to each year's contributions, not to the total amount you can contribute over your lifetime. So, if you don't use all of your FHSA room in a given year, you can carry it forward to future years. This means that if you have unused room from previous years, you can contribute more than the annual limit in a year when you open your first FHSA, as long as you don't exceed the total lifetime limit of $40,000. However, it's important to note that you can only contribute to an FHSA if you have a qualifying first home purchase or if you are 40 years old or older and have never owned a home. If you are under 40 and have never owned a home, you can only contribute to an FHSA if you have a qualifying first home purchase. 

For example, let's say you are 25 years old and you want to start building up your FHSA room. You can contribute up to $8,000 per year (10% of the $80,000 limit) to your FHSA, even if you don't plan to buy a home for several years. If you contribute $8,000 each year for 5 years, you will have built up $40,000 in unused room. Then, when you are 30 years old and decide to buy your first home, you can use this $40,000 of unused room, plus the $8,000 you can contribute in that year, for a total contribution of $48,000. 

However, if you are under 40 and have never owned a home, you can only use this built-up room if you have a qualifying first home purchase. If you don't have a qualifying purchase, you won't be able to use the built-up room until you turn 40 or have a qualifying purchase. 

It's also important to note that if you have a qualifying first home purchase and you withdraw money from your FHSA to buy or build a home, you won't be able to re-contribute that amount to your FHSA. But you can continue to contribute to your FHSA up to the annual limit each year, as long as you have unused room. 

In summary, you can build up unused FHSA participation room in years before you open your first FHSA, but you can only use this room if you have a qualifying first home purchase. If you are under 40 and have never owned a home, you can only use the built-up room if you have a qualifying purchase.

- The 10% limit on FHSA contributions applies to each year's contributions, not to the total amount you can contribute over your lifetime.
- You can only use the built-up room if you have a qualifying first home purchase.
- If you are under 40 and have never owned a home, you can only use the built-up room if you have a qualifying purchase.
- If you withdraw money from your FHSA to buy or build a home, you won't be able to re-contribute that amount to your FHSA, but you can continue to contribute up to the annual limit each year as long as you have unused room.
